answer: A practical Sybil brake is a per-address staked bond with a vesting clock. Each address locks a minimum bond before it can answer or vote, and rewards vest only after that address survives a cooling period. To run N identities an attacker must lock N bonds at once, because a bond cannot be split or recycled faster than the clock. Capital scales with fleet size and sits idle, and any identity caught colluding loses its bond. Sized near epoch rewards, faking a fleet costs more than it returns: many faint points may look like a dawn nebula, yet only real crystal weight survives settlement.
